routes.label: An isosceles triangle at the center

question:
Square \(ABCD\) is rotated \(20^\circ\) clockwise about its center to obtain square \(EFGH,\) as shown below. What is the degree measure of \(\angle EAB?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2023_AMC_10B_Q07_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Join \(A\) and \(E\) to the common center \(O\). This makes the rotation angle part of a triangle whose two sides are equal.

Because the rotation takes \(A\) to \(E\), it gives \(OA=OE\) and \(\angle AOE=20^\circ\). Triangle \(AOE\) is therefore isosceles, so its equal base angles are
\[
\angle EAO=\frac{180^\circ-20^\circ}{2}=80^\circ.
\]
The segment \(AO\) lies along a diagonal of square \(ABCD\). A square's diagonal bisects its \(90^\circ\) vertex angle, giving \(\angle BAO=45^\circ\). For the clockwise placement shown, ray \(AB\) lies between rays \(AE\) and \(AO\). Thus
\[
\angle EAB=\angle EAO-\angle BAO
=80^\circ-45^\circ=\boxed{35^\circ},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
